steps.title: Register the raw notes as the only source (and any earlier records)
do: The raw notes come from Paul: pasted into the chat or attached. Write them to a text file exactly as given (never tidied, never shortened) and register them: python3 {scripts}/run.py notes {run} --file <that file> --route pasted      (or --route device|m365|zapier after logging the try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --purpose notes --route device|m365|zapier --result found|failed --note "what you did")
Earlier Client Records of the same client that Paul gives you (for the duplicate check): python3 {scripts}/run.py earlier {run} --id e1 --file <the earlier .md> --route pasted
The program splits the notes into dated entries and says how many it recognised. No other source is used: never fill a gap from memory or a guess.
steps.proof: the raw notes are registered and unchanged, any route is logged in order, and the entries are counted

steps.title: Read the raw notes completely, in order
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}  and read the part it shows, completely. Then acknowledge it with one line on what is in it: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run} --ack 1 --note "..."  Repeat until every part is acknowledged. Searching for keywords is not reading.
steps.proof: every part of the raw notes was served in order and acknowledged

steps.title: Check for an earlier record of the same client; Paul decides
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py duplicate {run} --decision merge|separate --said "Paul's words"  ONLY when the program says an earlier record matches. Show Paul both and ask; never merge silently. When nothing matches, the program says there is nothing to decide.
steps.proof: no earlier record matches, or Paul's decision is recorded in his own words

steps.title: Enter the Client Record as ONE data file; the program checks it against the raw notes and draws the .md
do: Write record.json as the reference page shows. Never write the Markdown yourself: the program draws it.

If it refuses, put every listed problem right in the file and run it again. Never argue with a refusal; never make a fact fit by inventing it. Keep what the notes hold (condensed), or list it in left_out with a reason Paul will see.
steps.proof: every field is checked against the raw notes, every verbatim item is character for character in them, nothing the notes hold is missing, and the Markdown is the program's

steps.title: Send the .md file in the chat (and a copy in the client's folder only if Paul asked)
do: Send out/<file name>.md in the chat as a downloadable file (never chat-only text), then record: python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} chat.sent yes

ONLY if Paul asked for a copy in the client's folder: record his words (receipt save.paul_said) and the folder path (receipt save.folder), save it by the routes in order, list the folder, save the listing to a file and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py save {run} --file <the saved listing>
steps.proof: the file was sent in the chat, and a saved copy (only if Paul asked) shows in the folder listing

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Put the short audit and the block for Paul it prints in your reply exactly as they are. Nothing longer. Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
